correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge13\), the alternating 16-face cross-polytope chain is an integral 3-cycle in the Alexander dual; the n translated cocycles are genuine integer cocycles and pair as the n-by-n identity with the translated cycles. At \(n\ge14\) the distinguished tetrahedron has no five-vertex coface, by an exhaustive symbolic distance case split; at \(n=13\) the two-term signed wrap correction cancels its unique five-coface. Evaluation gives a cyclic-equivariant section of integral \(H^3\) onto \(\mathbb Z[C_n]\). At n=12 the explicit 12-term integer cocycle is checked on all 168 five-faces and evaluates -1 on the sphere cycle. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality transfers a split free summand to the next-to-top cut-complex homology. The standalone verifier exactly enumerates faces, signed cocycles, translation pairings and GF2 ranks (\(n=12\) 2, \(n=13\) 14); the all-n conclusion is proved by the finite symbolic cases, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The fully read 2026 cycle-power paper treats \(k=3\) and explicitly raises the \(k\ge4\), \(p\ge3\) question, without computing this cyclic regular module. The fully read 2023 foundational paper gives shellability inheritance under induced subgraphs, which, COMBINED WITH the fully read published four-cut cubic-PATH theorem, already implies plain non-shellability of cubic cycles; this assertion is explicitly excluded from the novel content. The published path theorem has only one split Z class, and induced-subgraph shellability inheritance does not give the original graph any global integral homology injection. The new n translated local cocycles, their unit off-diagonal-zero pairing, and wrapped \(n=13\) correction establish an equivariantly split rank-n module absent from that implication. Prior cyclic character calculations concern 3-cut rather than 4-cut complexes. No exact or stronger rank-n coverage was found in the named actual searches, but unindexed equivalence remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent cyclic regular-module result may exist beyond the inspected literature and searchable records.
The complete integral group could contain additional free or torsion summands; neither the theorem nor the supplementary finite ranks assert their absence.

The cubic-path construction supplies a related local obstruction, so the novelty rests on independence of all cyclic translates and the \(n=13\) wrap correction, not on the existence of nonshellability.

value.rationale: The source identifies higher cut complexes of cubic cycles as a motivated open territory. Quantifying a full regular lattice of n primitive classes, rather than only a shellability obstruction or one path-induced class, gives structural integral and equivariant information across an infinite natural family. The new wrapped-cycle \(n=13\) two-term correction yields n independent classes already below the simple path-folding threshold; the n=12 primitive cocycle and exact small mod-two ranks identify a genuine boundary phenomenon. This is not an arbitrary slice, restatement, or trivial exercise. It does not claim an overall exact homology classification.
